otel-offpath-f-nolag-v1.keptInTheReader: every rule of the reader: calibration, level rules, appear/absent, pass rule, cost model, lane rules (V33_LANE_RULES otel, unchanged; the `lag` lane is defined by service kafka, channel metric, metric-name prefix kafka.consumer_group.lag and is simply empty here)

parameters.origin_ref: design.ablation of pipelines/campaigns/otel-offpath-f-nolag-v1.json at 4ab4433 (designEpoch, removed, kept) and candidate_offpath_f_nolag.ABLATION_REMOVED. The integrity check is an engineering default of this file (a reporting row; it changes no calibration, rule, placement or score): the lag lane of v3.3 is the only lane the removed receiver fed, so a lag-lane sensor in an ablation cell would mean the receiver ran and the cell is not an ablation cell. Declared prediction FNL-L3 (PREDICTIONS_OVERNIGHT_20261014.json): the lag lane reads `—`, a lag id in the calibration would mean the ablation did not remove the receiver.

parameters.name: V35_REPORT_RULE
parameters.value: Admission and reporting only. v3.5 admits otel-offpath-f-nolag-v1 beside the epochs v3.3 admits (v3.2's, v3.3's) as a campaign-E-role epoch with F's profile; any other epoch is refused as in v3.3 (UnknownSchema), the epochs of the registries are never read two in one run (v3.2 ONE_NEW_EPOCH), and any system but otel is refused (Hotel is v3.4's, TeaStore's off-path epoch v3.3's). The readout carries, per ablation epoch read, the lag-lane integrity record: valid cells of the epoch, cells with a collected lag-lane sensor, the sensor keys, and `ablationHolds` (true iff no cell collected one); the coordinator lane (kafka log ids) and every other lane are v3.3's `v33.lanes` block, unchanged. Scope: method; no number is produced by the reader and no ablation claim is made by this rule.
